details:
Project Details: APOGEE

What it does & how it works: APOGEE is a browser-based aerospace simulator where players pick a launchpad on a 3D Earth, snap together a modular spacecraft from 27 parts, and pilot it from Earth to the Moon and onto the exoplanet GL-1500 using a real-time 120 Hz physics engine.

Benefits: It helps students actually see and test how rocket physics works—like weight, thrust, drag, and weather—right in a browser without needing to download anything.

Intended impact: We want to get other students excited about space exploration, coding, and engineering by letting them build and test their own rockets.

Tools & languages: We coded the whole project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with HTML5 Canvas for graphics, Web Audio for sound effects, and a browser so it runs on normal school laptops and tablets.

Creativity: Instead of using pre-made images or sound files, we programmed every rocket part, flame, explosion, and engine sound directly in code.

Key factors considered: We made sure the physics felt realistic without being too hard to play, kept the frame rate smooth, and built a step-by-step live tutorial so anyone can learn how to fly.
